title: Excitation energy funnelling in NIR-emissive [YbPrYb] heterometallic complexes

synthesis.procedure: Previously reported analogue used as a luminescence control. The SI states that [Yb2La(LA)2(LB)2(py)(H2O)2]NO3 (1) was prepared according to procedures previously published by the group; no quantities or steps are given in this article or its SI.

properties.summary: In 10^-4 M 1:1 MeOH-d4/DMSO-d6, 400 nm excitation gives only Yb3+ 2F5/2→2F7/2 emission centred at 980 nm. At 77 K the emission resolves into the four Kramers components of 2F7/2, matching the solid-state spectrum and the C2v geometry about the Yb sites. Observed lifetimes are 16 μs (RT) and 21 μs (77 K). Used as the unquenched Yb reference for energy-transfer efficiencies of complex 3.

synthesis.procedure: Main text: formed like [YbPrYb] from stoichiometric Yb-analogue reagents in eqn (1), with homogeneous crystals only when one equivalent of CuCl is added as a non-incorporated crystallization modulator; crystal yield about 15% (details in the SI). SI: a yellow pyridine solution of H2LA (14.8 mg, 0.032 mmol) and H2LB (10.2 mg, 0.032 mmol) in pyridine (10 mL) was added dropwise with stirring to a light-blue pyridine solution (10 mL) of Pr(NO3)3·5H2O (7 mg, 0.016 mmol), Lu(NO3)3·5H2O (14.4 mg, 0.032 mmol) and CuCl2·2H2O (2.7 mg, 0.016 mmol). The green solution was stirred for 1 h and layered with hexane. Green [Cu(py)4(NO3)2] crystals formed after one week; large orange crystals of 2 formed after one month and were separated. Yield ~15%. Elemental analysis for 2·3.1H2O and ICP Pr/Lu molar ratio 0.47 (calc. 0.50).
synthesis.time: stirred 1 h; crystals after one month
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange crystals separated from earlier green [Cu(py)4(NO3)2] crystals after hexane layering.

properties.summary: NIR emission is almost exclusively from Pr3+ 1D2. At 77 K, bands are assigned at 861 nm (1D2→3F2), about 1022 nm (1D2→3F3,4) and 1480 nm (1D2→1G4), with only a weak visible 1D2→3H4 feature near 607 nm. Table 1 lifetimes at 1020 nm are 0.04 μs (RT) and 0.30 μs (77 K); the narrative reports 0.03 μs and 0.4 μs for the same experiment. Solid-state 77 K emission matches solution. Dc susceptibility (3000 Oe, and 200 Oe from 2–30 K) gives χT ≈ 1.33 cm3 mol−1 K at 300 K, a 1.29–1.33 plateau from 300–200 K, and 0.05 cm3 mol−1 K at 2 K, approaching zero as expected for a single Pr3+ ion; magnetization at 2 K reaches 0.276 N_A μ_B at 7 T. No significant exchange is inferred.

synthesis.procedure: Main text proposes 2 Yb(NO3)3 + Pr(NO3)3 + 2 H2LA + 2 H2LB + 2 H2O + 9 py → [Yb2Pr(LA)2(LB)2(H2O)2(py)]NO3 + 8 HpyNO3, with crystal yield only about 15%. Homogeneous crystals of 2 or 3 require one equivalent of CuCl as a crystallization modulator that is not incorporated (SI for details). SI: orange crystals of 3 (yield ~15%) were obtained by the same method as 2, using Pr(NO3)3·5H2O (7 mg, 0.016 mmol), Yb(NO3)3·5H2O (14.4 mg, 0.032 mmol) and CuCl2·2H2O (2.7 mg, 0.016 mmol), i.e. ligands in pyridine added to the metal/Cu solution in pyridine, stirred 1 h and layered with hexane. ICP Pr/Yb molar ratio 0.50.
synthesis.time: stirred 1 h; crystallization over about one month (same approach as 2)
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange crystals separated from copper-pyridine nitrate crystals.

properties.summary: 400 nm excitation produces only Yb3+ emission at 980 nm; Pr3+ emission seen for [LuPrLu] is absent, indicating essentially quantitative Pr3+→Yb3+ transfer (ΦET = 1.00 at RT and 77 K). Yb lifetimes collapse to 0.10 μs (RT) and 0.09 μs (77 K) versus 16 and 21 μs for [YbLaYb], giving Yb3+→Pr3+ back-transfer efficiency 0.99 at both temperatures and subsequent non-radiative decay of Pr. Spectral overlap supports FRET from Yb 2F5/2 to Pr 1G4. Dc data (3000 Oe; 200 Oe at 2–30 K): χT falls from 6.23 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K (below the 7.26 expected for two Yb3+ plus one Pr3+) to 2.59 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K. Magnetization at 2 K rises quickly to about 3.3 N_A μ_B by 3 T, then more slowly. Subtracting the [LuPrLu] data indicates no significant intramolecular exchange.
